questions.prompt: Cicero, the consul, saved the city from great danger.
questions.answer: Cicerō cōnsul urbem ā magnō perīculō servāvit.

questions.prompt: We admired the works of Herodotus, the father of history.
questions.answer: Opera Hērodotī, patris historiae, admīrātī sumus.

questions.prompt: Flattery, the promoter of vices, deceives foolish men.
questions.answer: Assentātiō, adjūtrīx vitiōrum, hominēs stultōs dēcipit.

questions.prompt: At Corinth, a city of Greece, the exiles remained a long time.
questions.answer: Corinthī, in Achāiae urbe, exsulēs diū mānsērunt.

questions.prompt: The soldiers, all the bravest of them, withstood the enemy.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs, fortissimus quisque, hostibus restitērunt.

questions.prompt: Alexander, king of Macedonia, conquered many peoples.
questions.answer: Alexander, Macedoniae rēx, multās gentēs vīcit.

questions.prompt: We read the letters of Cicero, the orator, with great pleasure.
questions.answer: Epistulās Cicerōnis ōrātōris magnā cum voluptāte lēgimus.

questions.prompt: The philosophers, all the wisest of them, did not fear death.
questions.answer: Philosophī, sapientissimus quisque, mortem nōn timēbant.

questions.prompt: He was born at Rome, the greatest city of the world.
questions.answer: Rōmae, maximā orbis urbe, nātus est.

questions.prompt: Hannibal, leader of the Carthaginians, crossed the Alps.
questions.answer: Hannibal, Poenōrum dux, Alpēs trānsiit.

questions.prompt: We honor Vergil, the greatest poet of the Romans.
questions.answer: Vergilium, maximum Rōmānōrum poētam, colimus.

questions.prompt: The citizens, each of the noblest, defended the republic.
questions.answer: Cīvēs, nōbilissimus quisque, rem pūblicam dēfendērunt.

questions.prompt: Numa, the second king, gave laws to the Romans.
questions.answer: Numa, secundus rēx, Rōmānīs lēgēs dedit.

questions.prompt: The memory of Cato, a most stern man, endures.
questions.answer: Memoria Catōnis, virī sevērissimī, permanet.

questions.prompt: He lived at Athens, a famous city of Greece, for many years.
questions.answer: Athēnīs, clārā Graeciae urbe, multōs annōs vīxit.

questions.prompt: Wisdom, the guide of life, leads us to virtue.
questions.answer: Sapientia, dux vītae, nōs ad virtūtem dūcit.

questions.prompt: Caesar, a most skilled general, defeated the Gauls in battle.
questions.answer: Caesar, imperātor perītissimus, Gallōs proeliō vīcit.

questions.prompt: The maidens brought gifts to Diana, goddess of the hunt.
questions.answer: Virginēs Diānae, deae vēnātiōnis, dōna tulērunt.

questions.prompt: Croesus, king of Lydia, was the richest of all men.
questions.answer: Croesus, Lydiae rēx, omnium hominum dītissimus erat.

questions.prompt: The gladiators, all the fiercest of them, scorned death.
questions.answer: Gladiātōrēs, ferōcissimus quisque, mortem contempsērunt.

questions.prompt: Tarquin, the last king, was driven from the city.
questions.answer: Tarquinius, rēx ultimus, ex urbe expulsus est.

questions.prompt: The fame of Homer, the prince of poets, is immortal.
questions.answer: Fāma Homērī, poētārum prīncipis, immortālis est.

questions.prompt: At Carthage, a wealthy city, the merchants gathered.
questions.answer: Carthāginī, in opulentā urbe, mercātōrēs convēnērunt.

questions.prompt: Concord, the ally of the citizens, strengthens the state.
questions.answer: Concordia, cīvium socia, cīvitātem cōnfirmat.
